I wrote the 30-minute lesson on O3 (context and memory in an agent) at `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`. I haven't opened it in a browser or measured its length. I estimate it at roughly 3,800–4,000 words, which would fit the 30 minutes.

**The win:** you can decide, for each piece of information in the makerspace assistant, whether it goes in the context, in saved notes, or in a document the assistant looks up on demand.

**What it covers, in order:**
- **Warm-up:** a recall question on the agent loop.
- **Context window:** what the model sees in one call, and why tool descriptions count toward it.
- **Between steps:** the program resends the whole transcript on every call. A worked cost example shows 9,000 tokens processed for a run that ends at 4,000, using made-up numbers.
- **When the window fills:** context rot, plus clearing old tool results, compaction and sub-agents.
- **Between sessions:** nothing survives unless it is saved outside the window and loaded back. The worked example is the student training-status record.
- **Retrieval:** chunking, embeddings plus exact-word matching, and retrieving up front versus letting the model search with a tool.
- **Sorting practice:** a faded exercise on what goes where, with a budget risk to name.
- **Format:** three figures and five practice checks with instant feedback.

**Sources:**
- The main source is Anthropic's [context engineering article](https://anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents).
- I also used the Claude [context windows docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) and [Contextual Retrieval](https://www.anthropic.com/research/contextual-retrieval).
- I read the first two pages in full. The third I only saw in search results, so its figures (35% and 49% fewer failed retrievals) come from the search summary, not a full read of the page.
- All three are in `RESOURCES.md`.

**Also written:**
- A five-item quiz, `quizzes/0002.json`, with its key in `keys/0002.json`. It's ready when you are.
- A one-page cheat sheet, `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html`.
- A `NOTES.md` update. It records new misconception ids M7–M9 and M3, which I reused from key 0001. M3 is the idea that memory is automatic.

I didn't write a learning record, because you haven't yet shown you understand this material.

Quiz 0001 still hasn't been graded (`submissions/s1.json` and `s2.json`). I can do that next if you want.

I can re-explain any part or go deeper, and I can let you take quiz 0002 here in the chat.
